# 2nd Capstone – Minting and Managing Tokens (WKT dApp)

Official Workshop:  
🔗 https://docs.iota.org/developer/workshops/minting-and-managing-tokens  
Platform: entity["blockchain_network","IOTA Network","layer1 dlt"]  
Language: entity["programming_language","Move","smart contract language"]  
Frontend Stack: entity["software_framework","React","javascript ui library"] + entity["software_tool","Vite","frontend build tool"]  
Integration Kit: entity["software_library","IOTA dApp Kit","web3 frontend sdk"]  

---

## 🧠 What This Capstone Actually Is (Architect View)

This is **not just token minting**.

It is a **complete token economy system** consisting of:

- Fungible token (WKT)
- NFT badge system
- Admin governance layer
- User engagement mechanics
- Event-driven blockchain architecture
- React dApp integration
- Unit-tested Move contract

This is closer to a **mini economic protocol** than a tutorial.

---

# System Architecture Overview

```
Move Smart Contract (token_contract.move)
        ↓
Shared Faucet Object (On-chain State)
        ↓
Frontend dApp (React + IOTA dApp Kit)
        ↓
User/Admin Wallet Interaction
```

---

# Core On-Chain Model

## 1️⃣ WKT – Fungible Token

Created during `init()`
- Symbol: WKT
- Supply: Minted dynamically via treasury cap
- Metadata frozen

---

## 2️⃣ WorkshopBadge – NFT

Contains:
- recipient
- minted_at
- workshop_id
- metadata URL

Acts as:
- Achievement proof
- Redeemable asset
- Auto-minted reward

---

## 3️⃣ Faucet – Shared Contract State

This is the **economic brain** of the system.

Stores:
- Treasury cap
- Admin address
- Daily claim tracker
- Coupon registry
- Badge issuance tracker
- Redemption tracker
- Auto-badge config

It is shared globally via:

```move
transfer::share_object(faucet);
```

---

# 🔐 Admin Control Layer

## Admin Capabilities

image_group{"layout":"carousel","aspect_ratio":"16:9","query":["admin dashboard web3 dark theme","web3 coupon management ui","nft minting admin panel web interface","web3 settings configuration dashboard dark theme"],"num_per_query":1}

Admin can:

- Add coupon codes
- Remove coupon codes
- Set auto-badge configuration
- Mint badges manually
- Transfer admin rights

Security enforced via:

```move
assert!(tx_context::sender(ctx) == faucet.admin, ENotAdmin);
```

This is **role-based authorization at contract level**.

---

# 👤 User Economic Layer

Users interact through:

---

## Daily Claim System

image_group{"layout":"carousel","aspect_ratio":"16:9","query":["crypto faucet daily claim ui dark theme","token claim button disabled web app","web3 reward claim interface","blockchain dapp claim tokens screen"],"num_per_query":1}

Rules:
- 10 WKT per day
- Based on UTC timestamp
- Enforced via table mapping

```move
let today: u64 = now_ms / 86400000u64;
```

Hard deterministic logic. No frontend trust.

---

## Coupon Claim System

- Admin registers coupon
- User redeems once
- Coupon usage tracked per user

Prevents:
- Replay
- Double use
- Invalid codes

Error model:
- `EInvalidCoupon`
- `ECouponAlreadyUsed`

---

# 🏅 Badge Economy

## Manual Minting

Admin → creates NFT → transfers to recipient

---

## Auto Badge Minting (First Payment)

image_group{"layout":"carousel","aspect_ratio":"16:9","query":["confetti celebration modal web app","nft reward notification popup","web3 payment success screen dark theme","blockchain badge earned animation ui"],"num_per_query":1}

Triggered inside `make_payment()` if:

- First outgoing payment
- Auto config set
- No prior badge issued

This is **state-conditional minting logic**.

---

## Badge Redemption

Users can:
- Burn badge
- Receive 30 WKT
- One-time redemption

Enforced via:

```move
assert!(!table::contains(&faucet.nft_redeemed, sender), EAlreadyRedeemed);
```

Circular economy loop:

Badge → Burn → Mint tokens

---

# 💸 Peer-to-Peer Payments

```
coin::split()
transfer::public_transfer()
```

Enforced:
- Balance validation
- Emits PaymentMade event
- Optional auto badge mint

This completes:
Token issuance → circulation → reward → redemption

---

# 🧪 Testing Discipline

Run:

```
iota move test
```

Tests cover:

- Admin authorization failures
- Double daily claim prevention
- Invalid coupon prevention
- Badge ownership enforcement
- Double redemption prevention
- Insufficient payment failure

This is **production-grade contract discipline**, not demo code.

---

# 🌐 Frontend Layer

Uses:
- Wallet connection via IOTA dApp Kit
- DevInspect for view calls
- React Query for state sync
- Radix UI for consistent theme
- Transaction building via `Transaction()` objects

Important architectural pattern:

Frontend never trusts itself.  
All validation is on-chain.

---

# 📊 Sequence Model (Conceptual Flow)

Admin deploys →  
Contract initializes →  
Faucet shared →  
Users claim →  
Users pay →  
Badges minted →  
Badges redeemed →  
Events emitted →  
Frontend reacts.

This is event-driven Web3 architecture.

---

# 🚀 Why This Capstone Matters for You

Partner — this is the first workshop that forces you to think in:

- Shared state architecture
- Token economy design
- On-chain authorization
- Event emission patterns
- Deterministic validation
- Frontend-chain separation

This is closer to your **Enterprise Kernel thinking** than previous workshops.

It introduces:

- Role-based access control
- State mutation protection
- Multi-feature contract layering
- Test-driven Move development

---

# 🧩 Extension (Platform Thinking)

The extension suggestion in the workshop hints at:

- Token factory pattern
- Multi-tenant token deployment
- Tiered NFT systems
- Time-based schedulers
- Creator analytics dashboards

That moves from:
Single dApp → Platform architecture.

---

# ⏱ Suggested Study Block (Per Your Learning Style)

You prefer structured 60–90 min blocks.

### Session Plan

1️⃣ 45 min — Deep read Move contract only  
2️⃣ 30 min — Draw your own state diagram  
3️⃣ 30 min — Identify invariants  
4️⃣ 45 min — Trace one full payment lifecycle  

Total: ~2.5 hours deep architecture study.

---

# 🧠 Big Question for You (Architect Mode)

If you were to integrate this into AUMNITY or your enterprise kernel:

- Would Faucet be a governance module?
- Should badge issuance be policy-driven?
- Can coupon logic become contract-based approvals?
- Can WKT become a reputation token?

This capstone is small.  
But its structure is scalable.

---

If you want next:

- I can extract pure contract invariants.
- Or we can design a hardened enterprise version.
- Or build a minimal version first inside IOTA tools only.

You decide direction.
